summary: Add visual graph reasoning and derivation practice to the otherwise strong constant-acceleration chapter.

improvements.where: note, after ## Key ideas; pack diagrams
improvements.why: M1-3.1 explicitly requires graphical solutions, but the chapter has no diagram; a turning-point velocity–time graph makes signed displacement and total distance visible.
improvements.what: Use graph_sketch for a straight velocity–time line crossing the time axis, with axes and turning time labelled and positive and negative areas identified. Add a short note explaining that signed areas subtract for displacement but magnitudes add for distance; embed the SVG.

improvements.where: note, after the velocity–time graph; pack diagrams
improvements.why: M1-3.1 names displacement–time, speed–time and acceleration–time graphs as well; the current lesson only describes their shapes in words.
improvements.what: Use graph_sketch to show a constant positive acceleration–time line and annotate its rectangular area as change in velocity; explain alongside it that the corresponding velocity–time graph is linear and displacement–time graph is quadratic. Embed the SVG.

improvements.why: Only one existing item asks Sketch, and no item tests transformation from an acceleration–time graph to a speed–time graph, a form used by Pearson WME01.
improvements.what: Add a structured Sketch item that starts with a piecewise acceleration–time graph and asks for a labelled speed–time sketch and distance by area; include a sign or zero-crossing case and a marking scheme. Add a misconception-based MCQ on acceleration–time signed area as change in velocity, rather than velocity itself.

improvements.why: The bank uses equations but never asks learners to Show that or derive a constant-acceleration relation from a graph.
improvements.what: Add a structured Show that item deriving $s=ut+	frac12at^2$ from rectangle plus triangle areas under a velocity–time line, stating $v-u=at$ and showing every step.

improvements.why: The learner's Save My Exams source lists five suvat equations while the note lists four, and explains that the time equations can be read from a velocity–time graph.
improvements.what: Add $s=vt-	frac12at^2$ as the fifth equivalent form, with one sentence showing it follows by substituting $u=v-at$ into $s=	frac12(u+v)t$. Add that the equations must be recalled in the exam.

improvements.why: Pearson's specification requires graphical solutions using all four graph types, and an official WME01 question asks for a speed–time sketch from an acceleration–time graph.
improvements.what: Add a short graph-conversion checklist: track initial velocity, integrate signed acceleration interval by interval, take the magnitude for speed, and mark times at which velocity changes sign. Paraphrase the sources.
